hist30_std: How wide the spread of heart rates has been over the last 30 minutes. A wide spread usually means the rate is swinging, most often from repeated decelerations. Not a FIGO concept, but the strongest single feature in this dataset.
histcum_mode: The single heart rate this fetus has spent more of labour at than any other -- its settled resting rate across the whole recording.
histcum_min: The lowest heart rate reached at any point since the recording began.
win_baseline_bpm: The resting heart rate over the last 30 minutes, with accelerations and decelerations excluded. FIGO normal is 110-160.
lwin_frac_below_110: The share of the last hour spent below 110 bpm, the bottom of the normal band.
cum_time_above_160_min: Total minutes spent tachycardic since the recording began. Sustained tachycardia can be an early compensation sign.
lwin_baseline_slope: Whether the resting rate is climbing or falling. A slow steady climb is invisible to any fixed threshold but is a recognised warning sign.
win_var_bandwidth: How much the heart rate wobbles around its own baseline, measured only between events so decelerations cannot inflate it. FIGO calls under 5 reduced and over 25 marked.
win_stv: Average change between consecutive 3.75-second epochs (the Dawes-Redman measure). Falls before most other signs of distress.
lwin_low_var_min_per10: How much of the last hour had variability under 5 bpm. A sustained run of flat trace is more concerning than a brief dip.
win_dec_n_per10: How often the heart rate is dipping right now.
lwin_dec_n_deep_per10: Decelerations that drop at least 60 bpm below baseline, which carry more oxygen cost than shallow ones.
cum_dec_area: Depth multiplied by duration, added up over every deceleration since the recording began -- the accumulated oxygen debt, not just what is happening now.
trd_min_since_dec: How long the trace has been quiet. Large values are reassuring.
lwin_acc_n_per10: Accelerations reflect an intact autonomic response and are reassuring.
cum_acc_time_sec: Total seconds spent in accelerations since the recording began.
win_uc_n_per10: Current contraction rate. More than 5 per 10 minutes is tachysystole, which shortens the recovery time between contractions.
cum_uc_per10: Contraction rate over the whole labour
Average contraction rate since the recording began.
trd_uc_rate_ratio: Contractions now vs this labour average
Above 1 means contracting faster than this labour has averaged -- labour is intensifying relative to its own norm, not to a textbook.
win_good_frac: The share of the last 30 minutes with usable FHR. Carried as a feature rather than used to exclude records, so poor recording shows up as an explicit contribution instead of silently biasing the score.
elapsed_min: How long this trace has been running. Time to delivery is NOT available -- the bedside does not know when the baby will be born.
mh_mat_age: The mother's age at delivery. A background risk factor, not a property of this trace, and constant for the whole labour.
mh_gravidity: How many times this woman has been pregnant, this one included.
mh_parity: How many births she has had before. First labours are longer and behave differently from later ones.
mh_diabetes: Diabetes recorded in the header (1 yes, 0 no). Associated with larger babies and with poorer placental reserve.
mh_hypertension: Maternal hypertension (1 yes, 0 no), which reduces placental perfusion and so the reserve a fetus has for contractions.
mh_preeclampsia: Pre-eclampsia (1 yes, 0 no): the same placental-perfusion problem, more advanced.
mh_liq_praecox: Membranes ruptured before labour established (1 yes, 0 no), which raises the risk of infection and of cord compression.
mh_pyrexia: Maternal fever in labour (1 yes, 0 no). Fever raises the fetal baseline on its own and often signals infection.
mh_meconium: Meconium seen in the liquor (1 yes, 0 no). Observed during labour, not from the trace, and a long-standing marker of fetal compromise.
